description: How a customer-side identifier becomes the sha256 digest that crosses to Traigent. Customer-chosen identifiers are content and never cross as text. The label map and the digest key stay on the customer machine.

digest.preimage: tfl1 U+001F role U+001F source U+001F canonical_id (UTF-8)

key.scope: one 32-byte key per (tenant, project), held by the customer
key.key_id: first 16 hex of HMAC-SHA256(key, 'tfl1-key-id'); carried in the bundle and manifest as digest_key_id
key.rotation: changes every digest: clusters do not carry over, so rotation or key loss means re-onboarding

global_rules: No case folding, no trimming, no other rewriting unless a source rule below says so.
An empty identifier, or one containing U+001F or any other control character (U+0000-U+001F, U+007F), is rejected locally and never digested.
The identifier is digested as a whole string; it is never split, truncated or logged.

boundary.identifier: repository identity: the declared repository id, else the git remote canonicalized by repository_remote_rules
boundary.note: A remote that carries credentials is content: userinfo is dropped before digesting. A declared repository id is used as is (NFC only) and must not be a URL.

principal.identifier: the agent identity: literal agent_name, else literal experiment_name (the deprecated alias; agent_name wins)
principal.pattern: any non-empty string without control characters

principal.identifier: the full IAM role or user ARN as IAM returns it
principal.note: ARN case is significant and is not folded.

credential.identifier: the access key id of a selected IAM user (roles have no listable long-lived keys)

test_key_notice: PUBLIC TEST KEY ONLY. test_key_hex exists so vectors are reproducible; it is public and must never be used to digest real identifiers or in production.

vectors.note: decomposed input; NFC makes it equal the composed vector

repository_remote_rules: Strip ASCII space and tab around the remote. Reject an empty value, any other whitespace or control character, and any backslash.

Accepted forms: scheme://[userinfo@]host[:port]/path[?query][#fragment] with scheme (case-insensitive) one of https, http, ssh, git, git+ssh, ssh+git; the scp form [user@]host:path (a form without a scheme whose host is followed by a colon, as git reads it: the text after the colon is always the path, never a port); and an already-canonical host/path with no port. Any other scheme (file, ftp, ...) is rejected. The scp form needs no dot in the host.
Drop everything from the first ? or # (query, fragment), then drop userinfo (everything up to the last @ in the authority). Credentials never reach the digest.

Host: lowercase ASCII; remove exactly one trailing dot, and reject a host that still ends with a dot afterwards. A host without any dot (git@forge:org/repo.git, localhost) is valid, in the scp form too. An IPv6 literal keeps its brackets, lowercased. No IDNA conversion. Reject an empty host.

Port: a port equal to the scheme default (https 443, http 80, ssh and git+ssh and ssh+git 22, git 9418) is dropped; any other port is kept as host:port; a port outside 1-65535 is rejected. The scp form has no port. The canonical output of a remote that keeps a port is not itself a valid input: re-derive from the raw remote.

Path: percent-decode escapes that stand for an unreserved character (A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~); uppercase the hex of every other escape (so %2f becomes %2F and is never decoded). Collapse runs of / to one /. Path case is preserved.
Then, in this order: strip leading and trailing /; remove one trailing .git (case-sensitive, so .GIT stays); strip trailing / again. Remove .git once only: repo.git.git becomes repo.git.
Reject an empty path and any path segment equal to . or ..
Canonical form: host[:port]/path (no scheme, no userinfo, no leading or trailing slash).
